github_issues.title: Memory leak: `WanI2VCrossAttention._fp8_cache` accumulates across prompts when transformer object is reused

github_issues.title: Blockswap (maybe) filling up the memory and the problem of Sageattn_3 working together with torch compile on wanvideowrapper1.4.7
github_issues.problem_summary: WanVideo BlockSwap causes unbounded system-RAM growth on Windows (96GB filled by ~3rd run, pinned-memory related), and sageattn_3 + torch.compile either OOMs, degrades quality, or reduce-overhead fails (cudaMallocAsync pool conflict on Windows). Self-resolved with detailed evidence, 0 comments.
github_issues.solution: OP self-confirmed workarounds with logs: run ComfyUI with --disable-pinned-memory and replace the WanVideo BlockSwap node with the older 'WanVideo Enhanced BlockSwap' node — this stopped RAM growth and enabled 1920x1024x61-frame generation on a 5060 Ti 16GB. For sageattn_3: use the per_block_mean sageattn3 mode (or keep SageAttention 2.2 for first/last steps); torch.compile reduce-overhead is blocked by Windows cudaMallocAsync pool limits (not fixable via --disable-cuda-malloc).

assessment.notes: Two intertwined problems: BlockSwap unbounded RAM (fix: --disable-pinned-memory + older Enhanced BlockSwap node) and sageattn_3+torch.compile conflicts (fix: per_block_mean mode; reduce-overhead unfixable on Windows). Self-resolved with logs, 0 comments, but multi-system and hard.

github_issues.title: Low CUDA efficiency with WanVideoSampler and solution.
github_issues.problem_summary: Low GPU utilization / heavy memory swapping during WanVideoSampler on VRAM-limited setups (720p 30f uses 6GB; attention memory design can't sustain 720p 100f on 8GB) — attention implementation keeps full K/V and doesn't chunk Q, so long-sequence attention is memory-bound.
github_issues.solution: OP's own fix (applied to comfy/ldm/wan/model.py in Comfy core): keep only complete K and V in memory and compute attention for Q in chunks — 720p/120f then fits in ~4GB with high CUDA utilization (~90min for 6 steps on RTX 5050). Commenter (redomsu76) corroborated the symptom on a 5060 Ti but the fix was never ported to the wrapper or confirmed by the maintainer.

assessment.notes: Attention memory-design fix verified by OP on device (chunk-Q, keep full K/V) but applied to Comfy core, never ported to wrapper or maintainer-confirmed; numbers may drift as core evolves.

github_issues.title: eager backend advertises int8_linear on MPS but dispatches to CUDA-only torch._int_mm

github_issues.solution: Community-validated fix in thread (Terralien-jp, confirmed by two other users): handle it in int8_linear by dequantizing the weight to activation dtype and running F.linear instead of falling back to fp32 inside fast_int8_mm (3.4x faster than the fp32 fallback, accuracy within int8 quantization error). Not merged upstream; unmeasured workaround: PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK=1 (Maxim-Mazurok).

assessment.notes: Eager backend advertises int8_linear on MPS but dispatches to CUDA-only torch._int_mm; community-validated dequant+F.linear fix, unmerged. All Apple Silicon int8 users hit it.

assessment.notes: Race in VBAR fault after eviction; commenter-confirmed retry patch works but no upstream fix; intermittent = hard to grade.

github_issues.title: [ROCm multi-GPU] account_free uses the current device instead of the allocation owner
github_issues.problem_summary: On Windows ROCm with 2+ GPUs visible, freeing a tensor allocated on GPU 0 while GPU 1 is current logs `account_free: could not account free` (119x in a real workload) because the free path searches the current device's allocation table instead of the owning device's, leaving per-device accounting inconsistent. Reproduced with a minimal probe; VBAR not required.
github_issues.solution: OP has a tested local fix (look up the actual allocation owner and perform the free/accounting on that owner's device/context) but it is not merged and no maintainer response is in the thread.

assessment.notes: Clear root cause (free path uses current device not owner) with OP-tested local fix; unmerged, no maintainer response.

github_issues.title: Segfault in `hostbuf_free()` during RAM-pressure cache eviction (`HostBuffer.__del__`)
github_issues.problem_summary: SIGSEGV inside aimdo.so hostbuf_free() when ComfyUI's RAM-pressure cache evicts a stale cache entry holding the last reference to a ModelPatcherDynamic, triggering HostBuffer.__del__; kills the process outright ~2s after a new prompt. Reproduced twice with identical stacks on 2x RTX 4090; 0.4.14 ships a byte-identical aimdo.so so is not a fix.

github_issues.title: [ROCM/Linux]: VBAR allocation fails on RDNA1
github_issues.problem_summary: On RDNA1 (gfx1010/gfx90c), comfy-kitchen HIP is unavailable ('architecture is not in the validated target manifest') and VBAR/dynamic VRAM fails; int8_convrot hits HIPBLAS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE. Maintainer states RDNA1 is not on the ComfyUI support roadmap — an unsupported-architecture limitation, not a workflow mistake.
github_issues.solution: Workarounds per Zakhrov (comments): ROCm 7.15+ gives partial RDNA1 support (Triton/flash attention still broken, outputs gray garbage on >SD1.5 models), run with dynamic VRAM disabled, use GGUF quants, and use ComfyUI-MultiGPU's Distributed Torch 2 for virtual memory offloading.

assessment.notes: RDNA1 explicitly unsupported per maintainer; answer is unsupported-arch + workarounds (ROCm 7.15, GGUF quants, ComfyUI-MultiGPU).

github_issues.title: Krea2 Prompt Enhancement causes NaN when enabling Dynamic VRAM on a gfx1030 (RDNA2) card.
github_issues.problem_summary: With Dynamic VRAM enabled on RDNA2 (gfx1030/gfx1031), Krea2 prompt-enhancement workflows produce NaN/black/garbage outputs (block 26), while the same model+prompt works without Dynamic VRAM; suspected memory corruption in the VBAR mapping path. Maintainer says RDNA2 isn't the focus and devs won't investigate.
github_issues.solution: Partial workarounds in thread: derfasthirnlosenick found --reserve-vram 2 temporarily fixed it (later regressed with display artifacts), and reports that adding a cuCtxSynchronize after set access in src/plat.h three_stooges (suggested via AI analysis) worked for them but was never submitted as a PR. MillanSiS confirms --disable-dynamic-vram avoids all of it. No upstream fix; maintainer explicitly declined.

assessment.notes: Suspected VBAR memory corruption on RDNA2; maintainer declined investigation; only unverified workarounds (--disable-dynamic-vram).

github_issues.title: torch bridge requires numpy at runtime but the package declares no dependency on it
github_issues.problem_summary: comfy_aimdo/torch.py builds tensors via torch.as_tensor(holder) on __cuda_array_interface__ objects, which requires NumPy; with numpy absent the bridge fails at runtime ('Numpy is not available') while pyproject.toml declares no runtime dependencies, so installs import fine but the tensor bridge is broken.

github_issues.title: can comfyui read bus interface load like gpu-z? when its more than 30, it slow down comfyui.
github_issues.problem_summary: Feature request: have ComfyUI monitor PCIe/bus interface load (or system-memory-fallback signals) and free VRAM when bus load stays high because the GPU is shared with a browser/other apps.

github_issues.title: [ROCm/Windows] vbar_allocate clamps every VBAR reservation to vram_capacity, exhausting the GPU address space after three models
github_issues.problem_summary: aimdo's vbar_allocate (src/model-vbar.c:222-227) clamps each VBAR VA reservation to vram_capacity, so on large-VRAM ROCm/Windows devices every model >=1/10 of device capacity reserves the full capacity of address space; three models (LTX video+TE+VAE) exhaust the ~256 GiB per-process GPU VA space and sampling fails with hipErrorOutOfMemory while 60-82 GB VRAM is free.
github_issues.solution: OP demonstrated that changing one multiplier in ComfyUI (the ModelVBAR(self.model_size() * 10, ...) reservation in model_patcher.py _vbar_get) takes peak usage on a 43 GiB LTX workflow from 26,978 MB to 81,522 MB and turns the hard failure into a clean run (OP-confirmed measurement in issue body). No upstream aimdo fix confirmed yet; merged PR #78 (NVML pressure and async pre-free clamping) was bot-linked as related but not confirmed to fix this.

assessment.notes: Excellent record: exact C lines + one-multiplier ComfyUI fix with OP-measured before/after numbers; great grading candidate.

github_issues.title: [ROCm/Windows] DynamicVRAM: gray image output with quantized models (INT4/GGUF); GGUF hangs before sampling
github_issues.problem_summary: With --enable-dynamic-vram on ROCm/Windows (RX 7900 XT), MiniMaxH3 INT4 convrot_w4a4 quantized model outputs a completely gray image (0.4.11 runs 10 steps in <1s, 0.4.13 computes but still gray), and the GGUF build of the same arch fills VRAM and hangs before step 1. Low-level HostBuffer->VBAR roundtrip verified OK; suspect QuantizedTensor geometry handling in ModelPatcherDynamic.load and detour-hook interference with the legacy load path.
github_issues.solution: No confirmed fix. Maintainer 0xDELUXA could not reproduce on RDNA4/Windows ROCm 10.1 + torch 2.14, asked OP to retest, and suggested W4A8 or int8_convrot are better quantization choices than GGUF/W4A4 (comment, unconfirmed by OP).

assessment.notes: Gray-output mystery with INT4/GGUF quants, no confirmed fix, maintainer could not reproduce; only speculative quantization advice.

github_issues.title: Fix CUDA 13.0 crash: replace Detours with manual hooks + fix RIP-relative overflow via near allocation
github_issues.problem_summary: On CUDA 13.0 (nvcuda64.dll returning real function bodies with 14-byte prologues), Microsoft Detours fails to install aimdo's 6 CUDA hooks (DetourAttach error 8, DetourAllocateRegionWithinJumpBounds returns NULL), causing an access-violation crash at ComfyUI startup in control.py init_devices.
github_issues.solution: OP (community contributor 'openwork') provides a full fix in the issue body: abandon Detours and implement manual x64 hooks (absolute indirect JMP 'FF 25 00 00 00 00 + 8-byte addr' trampoline), plus fix RIP-relative displacement overflow via near allocation; validated 7+ days of daily use without crashes. Author caveats the fix may only apply to their own case; not confirmed merged upstream.

assessment.notes: Deep binary-level fix (manual x64 hooks vs Detours, RIP-relative near alloc) validated 7+ days by author but single-user, unmerged.

github_issues.title: [ROCm] DynamicVRAM failed to initialize: funchook_prepare(cuMemAlloc_v2) failed: 8 Failed to allocate memory in unused regions
github_issues.problem_summary: Running ComfyUI with --enable-dynamic-vram inside an AMD ROCm PyTorch Docker container (rocm7.2.2 image, RX 9070 XT), funchook fails to allocate trampoline memory near cuMemAlloc_v2 so DynamicVRAM init fails and ComfyUI falls back to legacy ModelPatcher. Container/environment-specific hook placement problem, not a workflow mistake.
github_issues.solution: Maintainer 0xDELUXA reports it works on the latest Windows ROCm via TheRock (7.15) with torch 2.12, Python 3.12, RDNA4 and asks whether OP tried just the --enable-dynamic-vram flag (comment); implies upgrading the ROCm/torch stack. No OP confirmation.

assessment.notes: Docker-specific funchook trampoline failure; implied answer is upgrade ROCm/torch stack; no OP confirmation.

github_issues.title: Win32 FILE_FLAG_SEQUENTIAL_SCAN has a feature/side effect of discarding data from OS cache after first access
github_issues.problem_summary: aimdo's Windows safetensors handling opens files with FILE_FLAG_SEQUENTIAL_SCAN, which makes Windows discard the cached data after first read; users with large RAM (512 GB) see models re-read from physical disk on every generation, and Bit-Nibble's PERFMON A/B test (aimdo build with vs without the flag) confirmed the flag causes repeated physical disk reads instead of OS-cache hits.
github_issues.solution: Fix merged via PR #76 (linked by maintainer rattus128 in comment: 'https://github.com/Comfy-Org/comfy-aimdo/pull/76'), flowed into comfy-aimdo then ComfyUI; brendanhoar confirms (2026-08-30 comment) 'This appears to be resolved from my perspective... the problem went away that day'. Additional OP-confirmed Linux workaround from VladiCz: adding --disable-pinned-memory (with --high-ram) restored ~10x faster model loads after ComfyUI 0.22.0.

assessment.notes: PERFMON A/B test + merged PR #76 + OP confirmation make this gold-standard ground truth; subtle Windows API semantics made it non-obvious to diagnose.

github_issues.title: A missing cuCtxSynchronize seems to be causing correctness issues or at least nondeterminism
github_issues.problem_summary: On a 4060 Laptop 8GB with Zeta-Chroma BF16 (~12GB, spills to dynamic VRAM), occasional one-step corruption ruins generations and same-seed runs differ; OP suspects vbar_fault evicts pages still in use by in-flight GPU work because eviction runs without a preceding synchronize (--disable-dynamic-vram removes the symptom).
github_issues.solution: OP's AI-assisted patch adding cuCtxSynchronize() at the top of vbar_fault appeared to fix it and OP posted fixed-seed sample sets, but maintainer rattus128 rebutted the theory (comment: unconditional sync in vbar_fault is a perf killer; vbars_free(budget_deficit(0)) already synchronizes conditionally; suggests LoRA nondeterminism). Coderabbit links merged PR #62 'Dev/double sync' as related; no explicit maintainer+OP agreement that the issue is fixed.

assessment.notes: Maintainer rebutted the OP's cuCtxSynchronize theory; workaround (--disable-dynamic-vram) confirmed but root cause unresolved and contested.

github_issues.title: ComfyUI start-up crash with sageattention2 installed
github_issues.problem_summary: With sageattention2 installed alongside comfy-aimdo (RTX 5090, CUDA 13.2, torch 2.12.0+cu132, ComfyUI 0.25.0), ComfyUI crashes on startup; removing sageattention2 or passing --disable-dynamic-vram both avoid it. Conflict between sageattention2's and aimdo's CUDA API hooking; coderabbit flagged issue #75 (CUDA 13.0 Detours hook failure) as a possible duplicate.
github_issues.solution: Workaround confirmed by OP in the issue body: launch with --disable-dynamic-vram (or uninstall sageattention2) and startup works 'perfectly well'. Root-cause fix (hook installation on CUDA 13.x) tracked via related issue #75; no maintainer fix confirmed in this thread (no comments).

assessment.notes: Multi-user-reproduced Triton rope kernel fault; fixed by PR #77 with OP confirmation; workarounds also documented.

github_issues.title: Access violation reading 0x00000000000000E0 - RX 9070 XT (gfx120X|RDNA4) ROCm 7.13 on Windows
github_issues.problem_summary: Intermittent 'Windows fatal exception: access violation reading 0x00000000000000E0' in aimdo vram_buffer.__init__ via get_aimdo_cast_buffer during CLIP text-encoder cast on RDNA4 ROCm 7.13 Windows (nightly torch 2.13.0a0); most reruns of the same workflow crash.
github_issues.solution: Commenter Apophis3158 attributes it to ROCm Windows' closed-source PAL (links ROCm/rocm-systems#6191 comment) and offers an unconfirmed ComfyUI patch: comment out STREAM_AIMDO_CAST_BUFFERS.clear() in model_management.py reset_cast_buffers(). No OP confirmation and no maintainer response.

assessment.notes: Blamed on ROCm Windows closed-source PAL; commenter's patch unconfirmed, no maintainer response, narrow RDNA4+ROCm-Windows population.

github_issues.title: hostbuf_file_reader_read failed with all mixed precision quantized video models on RTX 5090 Laptop
github_issues.problem_summary: All mixed-precision quantized video models (LTX-2.3 FP8, Wan2.2, Wan2.1, MiniMax H3 int8_convrot) fail at first sampling/prefetch with 'RuntimeError: hostbuf_file_reader_read failed' on Windows RTX 5090/2080 Ti. github_issues.solution: No fix; confirmed workarounds from commenters: --disable-async-offload (Hz198111: video generates successfully, just slower) or --disable-dynamic-vram; linesss found only restarting ComfyUI before each generation works reliably since the failure hits the re-stage path, and their --disable-async-offload/--disable-dynamic-vram/--disable-mmap attempts still crashed on the text-encoder load path. Maintainer asked for stack traces; thread unresolved.

assessment.notes: Multi-user confirmed but thread unresolved; only partial workarounds (--disable-async-offload / --disable-dynamic-vram), one user needs restart-per-generation.

github_issues.title: How to disable CUDA and to run on PyTorch?
github_issues.problem_summary: On FreeBSD (CUDA-unavailable platform, packaging FreeBSD ports), comfy-aimdo fails to load its .so and ComfyUI then dies with 'AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled' in model_management get_torch_device unless launched with --disable-dynamic-vram --cpu. Platform/torch-build limitation, not a workflow mistake.
github_issues.solution: Maintainer rattus128 explains the 'failed to load' message is expected and by design — ComfyUI is meant to fall back to non-aimdo execution in full for unsupported platforms. OP confirms ComfyUI works fine with the flags --disable-dynamic-vram --cpu on the CUDA-less torch build.

assessment.notes: Maintainer-explained by-design fallback; answer is just the flag combo --disable-dynamic-vram --cpu on CUDA-less torch; FreeBSD-only population.

github_issues.title: bug & fix: ModelVBAR crashes on NVIDIA GRID / vGPU instead of falling back
github_issues.problem_summary: On NVIDIA GRID/vGPU (RTX6000-24Q, A40-24Q), ModelVBAR(self.model_size()*10) raises a hard MemoryError('VBAR allocation failed') during model load because cuMemAddressReserve-based VBAR allocation fails in virtualized environments, instead of degrading gracefully to standard model management. Affects all vGPU/virtualized-GPU users; another user reports PyTorch >2.8.x correlation.
github_issues.solution: Maintainer rattus128 built a new wheel (actions run 23231132334) with a startup self-test that probes the required CUDA APIs and wholesale disables the DynamicVRAM system when they fail; OP gregdotcom confirms 'Thanks for the new build, working fine now' with full success logs. Maintainer notes --novram mode is similar but switches aimdo off entirely, and suggests a no-vbar DynamicVRAM mode belongs in core ComfyUI.

assessment.notes: Maintainer-built wheel with API-probe graceful fallback, OP-confirmed with logs; affects all vGPU/virtualized-GPU users.

github_issues.title: vGPU windows can't use comfy-aimdo
github_issues.problem_summary: On Windows vGPU (and SR-IOV vGPU guests like L40S-48Q on Proxmox), cuMemAddressReserve returns error 801 'operation not supported' — NVIDIA confirmed Windows vGPU cannot open UVM and the hypervisor does not expose the VMM APIs — so VBAR/DynamicVRAM can never initialize there and cloud-provider Windows users are affected.
github_issues.solution: Maintainer rattus128 shipped a wheel adding cuInit() plus an init-time probe of the required features so ComfyUI falls out of DynamicVRAM mode completely when they fail (comment with actions run 23231132334); Aanerud confirms 'The graceful fallback is working perfectly — ComfyUI no longer crashes, it just runs without Dynamic VRAM' and that the API is simply not exposed to vGPU guests (hypervisor-level restriction, not fixable client-side).

assessment.notes: Hypervisor-level restriction (NVIDIA-confirmed) with maintainer-shipped graceful fallback, user-confirmed working; near-duplicate of #25 (Linux vs Windows vGPU).

github_issues.title: MiniMax H3 Memory Efficient SageAttention hard-crashes on NVIDIA L20 / SM89 with FP8 path; FP16 SageAttention works
github_issues.problem_summary: MiniMax H3 generation in ComfyUI via KJNodes' MiniMaxH3MemoryEfficientSageAttentionPatch hard-crashes the CUDA context on SM89 (L20) inside the int8-QK/FP8-PV kernel path (_sageattn_int8_fp8_nhd); KJNodes PR #748 V-offset fix does not help.
github_issues.solution: OP A/B confirmed a settings-level workaround: switch the 'Patch Sage Attention KJ' mode to sageattn_qk_int8_pv_fp16_cuda and the same workflow runs cleanly — crash is specific to the SM89 FP8-PV kernel, which remains unfixed upstream.

assessment.notes: OP A/B confirmed settings-level fix (switch SageAttention patch mode to fp16-PV CUDA path); SM89-specific FP8 kernel bug remains unfixed upstream. KJNodes patch node involved.

github_issues.title: Support for PyTorch 2.14
github_issues.problem_summary: SageAttention does not build against PyTorch 2.14 because the repo's setup.py still compiles with -std=c++17 while newer torch requires C++20; issue body contains a ready setup.py patch.
github_issues.solution: Body proposes the exact fix: change CXX_FLAGS and NVCC_FLAGS in setup.py from -std=c++17 to -std=c++20. Unconfirmed by anyone and no PR merged.

assessment.notes: Trivial flag change (-std=c++17 -> c++20) but unconfirmed by anyone; grade as direction, near-certain correct.

github_issues.title: [Bug][sm_120][Windows] Driver-level GPU lost during MiniMax H3 generation with int8-QK/FP8-PV kernel on RTX 5060 Ti; native attention control passes at higher load
github_issues.problem_summary: MiniMax H3 generation with the int8-QK/per-channel-FP8-PV Sage kernel (_sageattn_int8_fp8_nhd) loses the GPU at the Windows driver level (nvlddmkm, requires reboot) on RTX 5060 Ti; a single-variable control shows native attention succeeds at higher VRAM/power, isolating the failure to the kernel.
github_issues.solution: OP-confirmed workaround (comment by leimuxiao, 2 clean 260s runs): keep int8-QK, demote V from per-channel FP8 to plain FP16 and call the sm80 kernel _qattn_sm80.qk_int8_sv_f16_accum_f32_attn instead of the sm89 fp8-PV kernel — no GPU loss, still ~21% faster than native. FP8-PV on this path remains broken upstream.

assessment.notes: OP-confirmed kernel-swap workaround (fp8-PV -> f16 V on sm80 path); true repro needs Windows RTX 50xx; fp8-PV path still broken upstream.

github_issues.title: gfx12 int8 kernel: fp16-V slower than fp16 sageattn at long sequences; fp8-V wins micro-benchmarks but no real-workload gain (RX 9070 XT)
github_issues.problem_summary: On RX 9070 XT (gfx12), the sageattn_qk_int8_pv_gfx12_native kernel is slower than plain fp16 sageattn at long sequences (1.31x at seq=8192), and the fp8-V mode that wins micro-benchmarks is 1.6-1.8x slower end-to-end in the real MiniMax H3 workload — the gfx12 kernel lacks the tuning of the NVIDIA _qattn_smXX kernels.

github_issues.title: [Bug] FP8 PV kernel produces silent noise corruption above ~160k sequence length on sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell)
github_issues.problem_summary: On sm_120 the FP8-PV kernel silently returns pure noise (no error) when packed MiniMax H3 sequence length exceeds ~160k tokens; identical configs below ~154k are clean and the SDPA control is correct at all lengths. Anyone running long H3 videos with SageAttention hits this.
github_issues.solution: No fix in thread; suspected FP8 PV accumulation/index overflow at large N. Only implicit avoidance is keeping total sequence length under ~160k or disabling SageAttention.

github_issues.title: int32 overflow in Triton kernels silently corrupts output (and sometimes crashes) for non-contiguous inputs at long sequence lengths
github_issues.problem_summary: Triton quant/attention kernels compute element offsets in int32; with non-contiguous q/k/v views into a fused QKV buffer (common pattern) the sequence-dim stride triples and offsets wrap past 2^31 at ~100k tokens, causing silent corruption then illegal memory access.
github_issues.solution: Root cause and fix direction identified in body: the sequence index (tl.arange/offset math) must be promoted to int64 as batch/head already are; no fix merged. Avoiding non-contiguous views (contiguous tensors) dodges it until ~300k tokens.

assessment.notes: int32 offset overflow root-caused in body; int64 promotion direction stated, no merged fix; silent corruption makes verification subtle.

github_issues.title: [SM89][Windows] Driver reset on very long HND attention; bounded-memory workaround
github_issues.problem_summary: On RTX 4080 16GB Windows/WDDM, the SageAttention2++ SM89 path at ~178k-token non-causal HND attention (Q/K/V views into one QKV allocation) loses the CUDA context with an nvlddmkm driver reset instead of a clean OOM; several full-size temporaries are alive simultaneously in the fp32+fp16 wrapper.
github_issues.solution: OP built and reports a working downstream memory-bounded wrapper around the same SM89 operator: fuse K-mean subtraction into per-thread int8 quant, two-stage V scale with direct fp8 layout write, 8-head group chunks, and 8192-token Q chunks. Not an upstream fix.

assessment.notes: OP-built memory-bounded wrapper is bespoke engineering, not an upstream fix; 178k tokens on 16GB WDDM is an edge case.

github_issues.title: per_channel_fp8 pads kv_len to 64 while sm90 kernel asserts pad to CTA_K=128 — direct callers of _qattn_sm90 abort at runtime
github_issues.problem_summary: API contract mismatch inside SageAttention: per_channel_fp8 pads kv_len to 64 but the sm90 kernels require padding to CTA_K=128, so any downstream caller using the memory-efficient direct path (e.g. KJNodes MiniMax H3 patch) aborts when kv_len % 128 is in [65,127].
github_issues.solution: Workaround: pad V to a multiple of 128 before per_channel_fp8, exactly as core.py's top-level sageattn_qk_int8_pv_fp8_cuda_sm90 already does (lines ~972-980). OP suggests fixing per_channel_fp8 to pad to 128 or adding a pad_to argument; KJNodes PR #729 filed; nothing merged upstream.

assessment.notes: Clean internal API-contract mismatch (pad 64 vs CTA_K 128); canonical pad-to-128 pattern already in core.py; KJNodes PR filed, not merged.

github_issues.title: SageAttention3 Blackwell per-block mean fails to initialize TMA descriptor at ~74k tokens on sm_120
github_issues.problem_summary: sageattn3_blackwell(per_block_mean=True) fails at ~73.8k-token sequences on RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120): TMA descriptor initialization error then illegal instruction, poisoning the CUDA context; per_block_mean=False on the identical tensors succeeds.
github_issues.solution: Comment by 258369977: fix implemented in PR #394 — detects the signed-int32 overflow in the per-block-mean delta_s TMA stride and evaluates aligned Q chunks while reusing K/V preprocessing; tested with regression coverage but not merged upstream. Body-confirmed workaround: per_block_mean=False.

assessment.notes: PR #394 (int32 TMA stride overflow) tested with regression coverage though unmerged; per_block_mean=False workaround body-confirmed.

github_issues.title: SageAttention3 (Blackwell FP4): low speedup on RTX PRO 5000 (sm_120, 110 SMs)
github_issues.problem_summary: SA3 FP4 shows no speedup over SA2-FP8 on RTX PRO 5000 (110 SMs) vs the paper's 1.8x on RTX 5090; Nsight Compute shows the FP4 kernel launches grid=(170,1,1) because sageattn3/blackwell/launch.h hardcodes the 5090's 170 SM count, causing wave quantization on smaller Blackwell SKUs.
github_issues.solution: OP-verified fix: replace the hardcoded 170 in launch.h with a runtime query (at::cuda::getCurrentDeviceProperties()->multiProcessorCount); after rebuild the grid becomes (110,1,1) and SM active utilization rises. Change not merged upstream.

assessment.notes: Hardcoded 170-SM grid in launch.h; OP-verified one-line multiProcessorCount fix with profiler evidence; affects all non-5090 Blackwell SKUs.
